title: Precision Asset Inspections — Final Round Bid Comparison
summary: Final round bid comparison for Precision Asset Inspections, Inc. prepared by ACP / William Blair in October 2021. title: Precision Asset Inspections — Management Presentation
summary: Final-round buyer management presentation for the exit sale of Precision Asset Inspections, Inc., a Houston-based technology-enabled NDT (non-destructive testing) and asset integrity management services company. Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II acquired Precision in January 2016 at $52M revenue and grew it to $142M LTM revenue by June 2021 through organic technology investment and three geographic bolt-on acquisitions. Key highlights include the proprietary Vantage IQ platform (AI-assisted defect detection, SaaS data subscriptions at $8.2M and growing 48% YoY), 3.3x EBITDA growth during the hold, expansion from 4 to 11 service centers, and a certified technician base of 620. The document outlines future growth opportunities including Rocky Mountain/Pacific Northwest expansion, offshore platform inspection, and utility transmission markets, prepared for final-round strategic/financial buyer management meetings in September 2021.

key_quotes.quote: AI-assisted defect detection reduces false-positive rates by 31% vs. manual interpretation and cuts reporting cycle time from 5 days to 4 hours.
The data subscription layer generates $8.2M in recurring SaaS revenue — growing at 48% per annum — and will convert all legacy inspection-only clients by 2023.

Precision has grown from a $52M regional inspection business to a $142M national platform across 11 service centers through organic technology investment and three targeted geographic bolt-on acquisitions.
Precision can onboard acquired companies' inspectors faster than any competitor can build an equivalent field team.
7 of the top 10 US midstream operators run Vantage IQ as their primary asset management system.

growth_drivers: Vantage IQ SaaS data subscription layer growing at 48% per annum with $8.2M in recurring revenue
Geographic roll-up via bolt-on acquisitions in Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian corridor
ASNT-accredited training center producing 80–100 certified technicians per year enabling fast integration
MSA book expanded from 42 to 162 active contracts during holding period
Rocky Mountain and Pacific Northwest expansion targeting $30–40M incremental addressable market
Offshore NDT platform inspection opportunity in $180M addressable Gulf of Mexico market
Utility transmission and power generation adjacent market of $220M
risks: Founder dependency on CEO Jim Harrington and CTO Dr. Aisha Okafor (co-founders with 13-year tenure)
SaaS revenue still represents a modest share of total revenue ($8.2M of $142M LTM)
Geographic expansion into Rocky Mountain and Pacific Northwest not yet executed
Integration risk from acquired bolt-on businesses

title: Precision Asset Inspections — Funds Flow Memorandum
summary: Closing funds flow memorandum prepared by Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP for the sale of Precision Asset Inspections, Inc. to Bureau Veritas at an agreed enterprise value of $310M. title: Precision Asset Inspections — HSR Filing Summary
summary: Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) filing summary prepared by Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher LLP for the acquisition of Precision Asset Inspections by Bureau Veritas S.A. at a transaction value of $310M. The transaction was reportable under HSR (exceeding the $92M size-of-transaction threshold). Both parties filed simultaneously on November 11, 2021; the DOJ Antitrust Division granted early termination on Day 18 (November 29, 2021), clearing the transaction to close. The deal closed December 15, 2021. Antitrust risk was limited due to minimal horizontal overlap between BV's building/construction focus and Precision's energy/pipeline focus.

key_quotes.quote: BV's US NDT operations are primarily in building/construction; limited overlap with Precision's energy/pipeline focus
The transaction presents manageable antitrust risk.
The DOJ granted early termination on Day 18, consistent with the parties' pre-filing analysis that horizontal overlap was limited.

risks: HSR reportability required formal filing and waiting period
Potential horizontal overlap with Bureau Veritas US NDT operations — assessed as limited

title: Precision Asset Inspections — Sell-Side Quality of Earnings Summary
summary: FTI Consulting Transaction Advisory Services prepared this vendor due diligence Quality of Earnings report for Precision Asset Inspections on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners / William Blair in support of the July 2021 sale process. The report presents an adjusted EBITDA bridge for LTM June 2021, lifting reported EBITDA of $26.4M to a preliminary adjusted EBITDA of $31.0M via $4.6M in addbacks (CEO comp normalization, M&A/integration costs, non-recurring legal/advisory, Vantage IQ R&D platform investment, phantom equity/SBC) less a $0.4M COVID revenue pull-forward adjustment, plus a $1.0M D&A reclassification. Key findings highlight excellent revenue quality (68% MSA-contracted, 94% renewal rate, no customer >8% of revenue), well-documented and conservative adjustments, lean working capital (NWC peg of $6.4M), and a rapidly growing SaaS revenue layer (Vantage IQ data subscriptions of $8.2M, +48% annually) with strong forward visibility.

key_quotes.quote: 68% of LTM revenue is under multi-year MSAs with remaining terms of 2–5 years. MSA renewal rate of 94% over the past 5 years. No single customer exceeds 8% of revenue.
Total addbacks of $4.6M against reported EBITDA of $26.4M are evidenced by third-party invoices and internal project tracking.

Vantage IQ data subscriptions ($8.2M, growing 48% annually) are recognized ratably over 12-month subscription terms... contracted subscription backlog of $9.4M provides strong forward visibility. This revenue layer carries 26% EBITDA margin vs. 18% for field services.

NWC as % of revenue is 4.2–5.1% — well below distribution-sector peers — reflecting the services nature of the business (no inventory; billings are milestone/completion driven). Proposed NWC peg of $6.4M reflects trailing-12-month average, which FTI confirms is conservative.

growth_drivers: MSA-contracted revenue base (68% of LTM revenue) with 94% renewal rate
Vantage IQ SaaS data subscriptions growing 48% annually to $8.2M
$9.4M contracted subscription backlog providing forward visibility
No single customer exceeds 8% of revenue — diversified base
risks: COVID-related revenue pull-forward ($0.4M timing benefit in H1 2021) may not recur
Integration costs from Appalachian Pipeline Testing acquisition
Phantom equity / SBC obligations settled at exit

title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation: Precision Asset Inspections, Inc.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund II entry IC memo recommending acquisition of Precision Asset Inspections, Inc., a Houston-based non-destructive testing (NDT) and asset integrity management services provider, at an $82M enterprise value (8.7x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $9.4M). The investment thesis centers on a geographic roll-up of regional NDT firms, commercialization of the proprietary Vantage IQ SaaS-like inspection platform, and EBITDA margin expansion from ~18% toward peer levels of 22–25%. The base case underwrites a 3.0x MOIC / 23% IRR at a $310M exit EV over a ~5-year hold, with identified bolt-on pipeline of 12 targets across Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian corridors.

key_quotes.quote: We underwrite a 3.0–4.0x MOIC over a 5–6 year hold through geographic roll-up of regional NDT firms, completion and commercialization of the Vantage IQ technology platform, and expansion into the adjacent offshore and utility inspection markets.

Precision's inspection revenue is therefore driven by regulatory calendars, not operator capex budgets. Revenue declined only 8% during the 2020 COVID shutdown — inspections were deferred, not cancelled, and catch-up drove a strong 2021 rebound.

We see a clear path to $5M+ annual SaaS subscription revenue by Year 4 as we migrate existing MSA clients onto the platform. Data switching costs and inspection history depth create durable retention.

The US energy infrastructure NDT market is served by ~400 regional firms with <$20M revenue each. We have identified 12 target acquisitions in the Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian pipeline corridors — the three highest-density NDT demand markets.

Precision's 18.1% EBITDA margin at entry is below the 22–25% margins of comparably scaled TIC peers (Bureau Veritas, Intertek). Margin expansion levers: (a) Vantage IQ reduces per-inspection labor cost by 20%+; (b) technician utilization improvement from 62% to 75–78%; (c) fixed-overhead absorption as revenue scales.

growth_drivers: Regulatory-mandated inspection demand (PHMSA, API standards) providing non-discretionary revenue base
Vantage IQ proprietary SaaS-like platform targeting $5M+ annual subscription revenue by Year 4
Geographic roll-up of 12 identified regional NDT targets in Permian Basin, Gulf Coast, and Appalachian corridor
Technician utilization improvement from 62% toward peer best-in-class 75–78%
In-house ASNT-accredited training center to scale certified technician pipeline
Expansion into adjacent offshore and utility inspection markets
risks: Vantage IQ platform delivery risk — 70% complete, requires $6–8M additional investment over 18 months
Energy sector cyclicality — 44% of revenue tied to oil & gas E&P and midstream operators
Technician labor scarcity — tight ASNT certification pipeline vulnerable to competitor poaching
Integration complexity across geographically dispersed bolt-on service centers
